drivingQuestion: What prompted R' Yosei's 'you examined me closely', and is his reading of R' Eliezer consistent?
outcomeNote: the Sages' challenge is rebuffed and the contradiction resolved by Rav Yosef's recension

segments.he: מַאי אָמְרִי לֵיהּ דַּאֲמַר לְהוּ דִּקְדַּקְתֶּם אַחֲרַי? הָכִי אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: הִגְבִּיהַּ בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת, מַהוּ? אֲמַר לְהוּ: דִּקְדַּקְתֶּם אַחֲרַי.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «What did they say to him that» led Rabbi Yosei to «say to them: You were diligent» to examine «my» opinion? The Gemara explains that «this» is what «they said to him: What is» the halakha in a case where one «lifted» an item «at twilight» between Shabbat and Yom Kippur and carried it from one domain to another? If the domains are adjacent, this act can be performed so quickly that even at twilight it does not span two days. For this reason, Rabbi Yosei «said to them: You were diligent» to examine «my» opinion.

segments.he: וְנֵימָא לְהוּ: מִקְצָת הַגְבָּהָה הָיְתָה מֵהַיּוֹם וּמִקְצָתָהּ לְמָחָר! הָכִי נָמֵי קָאָמַר לְהוּ: דִּקְדַּקְתֶּם אַחֲרַי, וְלֹא הֶעֱלִיתֶם בְּיֶדְכֶם כְּלוּם.
segments.en: Since according to Rabbi Yosei the period of twilight is instantaneous, the Gemara objects: «But let him say to them:» In this case as well, «part of the lifting was» performed «today and part of it was» performed «tomorrow.» The Gemara explains: «That is also what he is saying to them: You were diligent» to examine «my» opinion, «and» yet «you have not accomplished anything,» as I remain steadfast in my opinion.

segments.he: וּלְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי גְּמַר מְלָאכָה, לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר פָּטוּר? הָא שָׁמַעְנָא לֵיהּ דִּמְחַיֵּיב! דִּתְנַן, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: הָאוֹרֵג שְׁלֹשָׁה חוּטִין בַּתְּחִלָּה, וְאֶחָד עַל הָאָרִיג – חַיָּיב!
segments.en: The Gemara objects: «And according to Rabbi Yosei,» had the start of the labor been on Shabbat and the «completion of» the «labor» on Yom Kippur, Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua would agree that he is exempt. But «according to Rabbi Eliezer,» would he really be «exempt? Didn’t we hear that» Rabbi Eliezer «deems» one «liable» for the final stage of a prohibited labor? «As we learned» in a mishna (Shabbat 105a) that «Rabbi Eliezer says: One who weaves» on Shabbat is «liable» to bring a sin offering if he weaves «three threads at the beginning» of work on a new item, «or» if he adds «one» thread «to» a preexisting «woven fabric.» Although the minimum number of threads required for the prohibited labor of weaving is generally three, Rabbi Eliezer deems one liable for a single thread that he adds to a woven fabric.

segments.he: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הָכִי מַתְנֵי, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: הָאוֹרֵג שְׁלֹשָׁה חוּטִין בַּתְּחִלָּה, וּשְׁנַיִם עַל הָאָרִיג – חַיָּיב.
segments.en: «Rav Yosef said» in response: «Rabbi Yosei, in accordance with» the opinion «of Rabbi Eliezer,» would explain that «this is» what the mishna «teaches: Rabbi Eliezer says: One who weaves» on Shabbat is «liable» if he weaves «three threads at the beginning» of work on a new item, «or» if he adds «two» threads «to» a preexisting «woven fabric.»
